newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends higher on overseas buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends higher on overseas buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher on Tuesday compared to New York's previous close on overseas buying from Europe following the upward trend by silver and platinum and on improved sentiment, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$349.30/80 an ounce against New York's US$348.00/50 close on Monday.
Morning trade saw gold sales from the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) on a stronger dollar/yen, dealers said.
But buying from Swiss and London-based traders pulled the market up in the latter half of the day.
"Sentiment has improved," said a senior precious metals trader.
Dealers said if gold could break above $350 per ounce, it could jump further to $354 or higher.
Local gold ended HK$15 higher at HK$3,233 a tael.
Physical buying had been dampened by firmer prices, dealers said.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil from its previous fix at -1.00
